quests.instruction: Which word describes the opposite direction on a family tree from your own future children?
quests.hint: One direction on a tree looks backward, the other looks forward — this word is the backward one.
quests.explanation: Ancestors describes the opposite direction on a family tree from your own future children, or descendants.
quests.funFact: A family tree can show both directions at once: ancestors above and descendants below!

quests.instruction: Which word could describe you and your siblings and cousins, as one age-based group?
quests.hint: This word groups relatives close in age together.
quests.explanation: Generation could describe you and your siblings and cousins, as one age-based group.
quests.funFact: Cousins are often part of the same generation, even though they have different parents!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the people you would count if asked how many live in your home?
quests.hint: This word matches your home address, not your whole family tree.
quests.explanation: Household describes the people you would count if asked how many live in your home.
quests.funFact: A single household can range from just one person to a dozen people or more!

quests.instruction: Which word describes just your parents and siblings, without aunts, uncles, or cousins?
quests.hint: This is the smallest, closest circle of your family.
quests.explanation: Immediate Family describes just your parents and siblings, without aunts, uncles, or cousins.
quests.funFact: The word 'immediate' means closest or nearest, which is exactly why this phrase fits!

quests.instruction: Which word could you use to show how a cousin and a sibling are both connected to you?
quests.hint: This tool visually maps out every family connection.
quests.explanation: Family Tree could be used to show how a cousin and a sibling are both connected to you.
quests.funFact: Drawing your own family tree is a fun way to see just how big your family really is!

quests.instruction: Which word means the people whose lives led to your own family existing today?
quests.hint: Without these relatives from the past, your family today would not exist.
quests.explanation: Ancestors means the people whose lives led to your own family existing today.
quests.funFact: Every single ancestor in your family line played a small part in your family's story!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the group you belong to along with your siblings and cousins, roughly the same age?
quests.hint: This word groups you with relatives close in age, not just close in blood.
quests.explanation: Generation describes the group you belong to along with your siblings and cousins, roughly the same age.
quests.funFact: Even distant cousins can belong to the very same generation as you!

quests.instruction: Which word describes everyone who lives together under the same roof?
quests.hint: This word is about who shares your home, not just who shares your blood.
quests.explanation: Household describes everyone who lives together under the same roof.
quests.funFact: A household can include family members, and sometimes even close family friends who live together!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the people you would list first if asked about your family?
quests.hint: These are usually the very first names that come to mind.
quests.explanation: Immediate Family describes the people you would list first if asked about your family.
quests.funFact: Most people can name their immediate family members instantly, without even thinking!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a drawing that shows how all your relatives are connected?
quests.hint: This word borrows its name from the shape of branches.
quests.explanation: Family Tree describes a drawing that shows how all your relatives are connected.
quests.funFact: A family tree is called a 'tree' because it branches out just like the branches of a real tree!

quests.instruction: Which word means every relative who came before you in your family line?
quests.hint: This word covers every generation that came earlier than yours.
quests.explanation: Ancestors means every relative who came before you in your family line.
quests.funFact: Tracing your ancestors is sometimes called 'genealogy,' a popular hobby for many families!

quests.instruction: Which word could describe your grandparents' whole age group, compared to your parents' age group?
quests.hint: This word separates one age-based group of relatives from the next.
quests.explanation: Generation could describe your grandparents' whole age group, compared to your parents' age group.
quests.funFact: Each generation often grows up with different technology, music, and popular styles!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a home and everyone living inside it, considered as one unit?
quests.hint: This word combines the home itself with the people inside it.
quests.explanation: Household describes a home and everyone living inside it, considered as one unit.
quests.funFact: Census forms often ask questions about an entire household at once!

quests.instruction: Which word means the smallest, closest circle of your family?
quests.hint: This circle usually fits around one dinner table.
quests.explanation: Immediate Family means the smallest, closest circle of your family.
quests.funFact: Your immediate family often shares your daily routines, like meals and bedtime!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a diagram often shaped like branches, showing generations of a family?
quests.hint: This diagram organizes relatives by generation.
quests.explanation: Family Tree describes a diagram often shaped like branches, showing generations of a family.
quests.funFact: Family trees can be drawn on paper, or even built using special computer programs today!

quests.instruction: Which word describes relatives who lived before you, like great-great-grandparents?
quests.hint: This word points backward in time, not forward.
quests.explanation: Ancestors describes relatives who lived before you, like great-great-grandparents.
quests.funFact: The word 'ancestor' comes from an old word meaning 'one who goes before'!

quests.instruction: Which word means a step on a family tree, separating parents from children?
quests.hint: This word describes the gap between one age level and the next.
quests.explanation: Generation means a step on a family tree, separating parents from children.
quests.funFact: Moving from one generation to the next on a family tree is like climbing a step on a staircase!

quests.instruction: Which word means the group of people, including family, who share one home?
quests.hint: This word focuses on the shared home, not just the family connection.
quests.explanation: Household means the group of people, including family, who share one home.
quests.funFact: The word 'household' comes from combining 'house' and 'hold,' meaning the people a house holds!

quests.instruction: Which word could describe a small family of just three or four people?
quests.hint: This phrase does not include more distant relatives.
quests.explanation: Immediate Family could describe a small family of just three or four close people.
quests.funFact: Families of every size, big or small, still have an immediate family at their core!

quests.instruction: Which word could show you exactly how many grandparents or cousins you have?
quests.hint: This chart lays out every relative and how they connect.
quests.explanation: Family Tree could show you exactly how many grandparents or cousins you have.
quests.funFact: Counting the branches of a family tree is a fun way to practice both family words and math!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the relatives at the very top of an old family tree?
quests.hint: On many family trees, this word fits the oldest branches shown.
quests.explanation: Ancestors describes the relatives at the very top of an old family tree.
quests.funFact: The further up a family tree you go, the further back in history your ancestors lived!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a group of people born around the same time, like all the grandparents in a family?
quests.hint: This word groups relatives by their age level, not their individual names.
quests.explanation: Generation describes a group of people born around the same time, like all the grandparents in a family.
quests.funFact: A generation usually spans about twenty to thirty years, though it can vary!

quests.instruction: Which word means your family, but specifically thought of as the people sharing your address?
quests.hint: This word centers on the shared address, not distant relatives.
quests.explanation: Household means your family, but specifically thought of as the people sharing your address.
quests.funFact: Two people can be in the same family but different households if they live in separate homes!

quests.instruction: Which word could describe the people shown in a simple family photo of just your household?
quests.hint: This is usually a small photo, not one with dozens of relatives.
quests.explanation: Immediate Family could describe the people shown in a simple family photo of just your household.
quests.funFact: Many families take a yearly photo of just their immediate family to mark how everyone has grown!

quests.instruction: Which word means a visual way to see your whole family's connections at once?
quests.hint: This is a picture, not just a list of names.
quests.explanation: Family Tree means a visual way to see your whole family's connections at once.
quests.funFact: Some very old family trees have been kept and added to for hundreds of years!

quests.instruction: Which word means family members from history, rather than family members alive today?
quests.hint: This word points to the past, not the present.
quests.explanation: Ancestors means family members from history, rather than family members alive today.
quests.funFact: Many museums have exhibits dedicated to helping people learn about their ancestors!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a group like 'all the grandparents' or 'all the grandchildren' in a family?
quests.hint: This word names an entire age-based layer of the family.
quests.explanation: Generation describes a group like 'all the grandparents' or 'all the grandchildren' in a family.
quests.funFact: You can describe a whole family by counting how many generations are shown on its family tree!

quests.instruction: Which word could include parents, children, and even a pet, all living in one place?
quests.hint: This word is about the whole home, not just the humans in it.
quests.explanation: Household could include parents, children, and even a pet, all living in one place.
quests.funFact: Many surveys ask how many people and pets live in a single household!

quests.instruction: Which word means the closest group of relatives who usually live in your own home?
quests.hint: Think of the people you share breakfast with most mornings.
quests.explanation: Immediate Family means the closest group of relatives who usually live in your own home.
quests.funFact: Some forms ask specifically about your immediate family instead of your whole extended family!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a project many students make for school, showing their own relatives?
quests.hint: This is a common classroom project about family connections.
quests.explanation: Family Tree describes a project many students make for school, showing their own relatives.
quests.funFact: Making a family tree project is a fun way for students to interview relatives and learn family history!
